messages.text: A feature brief seeding the Pathly pipeline for LocalUsageMeter, a local, offline, per-developer tool that reads Claude Code and Codex CLI session logs to show today's token usage and cost against a daily budget. It matters because provider consoles lag by 1–2 days, leaving developers blind to same-day spend.
feature consultation started…

A real scrubbed sample log file (~/.claude/projects/<proj>/<session>.jsonl) is required for BUILD/TEST to validate parsing against the actual format. ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSAL.md defines the complete technical design for local-usage-meter: a greenfield TypeScript/Node.js tool with a daemon+reader split, ccusage embedded behind a compatibility port, incremental JSONL tailing with periodic full recompute, and a dumb statusline script reading a 2KB atomic snapshot. Ten sections covering stack, module layers, data model, real-time strategy, statusline integration, phase sequencing, ADRs, risks, and pre-build prerequisites.

DEDUP IS MANDATORY before aggregation: Claude Code duplicates assistant messages across session files on resume/compact (causing 2–3× inflation); Codex total_token_usage is cumulative per session (summing it inflates). Dedup keys are message.id+requestId (Claude Code) and session file + last seen cumulative value (Codex). Any aggregation that skips dedup will overcount by 2–3×.

The statusline is designed to self-spawn the daemon when it finds a stale snapshot (throttled, detached, fire-and-forget) — zero-configuration, but a background process appears without explicit consent. Alternative: require an explicit `lum service install` (launchd/systemd). Proceeding with self-spawn (ADR-002) since the brief says setup is trivial, but flagging for human override.

# Human Questions — local-usage-meter

_Raised by: architect · Stage: DESIGN (storm) · 2026-08-10_
_Context: `ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSAL.md`. Each question has a fallback assumption already baked into the
proposal, so BUILD is not blocked on an answer — but a different answer changes what is listed._

---

## ARCH_QUESTION
Question: How should the tool know whether a CLI is on a subscription plan (no marginal cost, so the
USD figure is imputed) versus an API-key account (real marginal cost)? The config schema in
PO_NOTES.md has `imputeCostForSubscription` (whether to impute) but no key declaring which kind of
account the developer actually has.
Options: (A) add an optional per-CLI `accountMode: { claude: "subscription"|"api", codex: ... }` key
that the developer sets once, defaulting to `"subscription"`; (B) always label every figure as
imputed (`≈`) and never claim a number is real spend; (C) auto-detect by probing for
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` env vars and CLI auth files.
Assuming: **(A) with default `"subscription"`** — the number is labelled imputed (`≈$3.20`) until the
developer explicitly declares an API-key account. Over-labelling as imputed is harmless; claiming
real marginal spend when there is none is misleading.
Impact: If (B), drop `accountMode` entirely and always render `≈` — simpler, but API-key users see a
hedge on a number that is exactly right. If (C), the tool must read environment and credential
locations, which cuts against the "nothing leaves the machine / touches nothing sensitive" posture
and is fragile (an env var can be set without being the active auth path) — I recommend against it.

---

## ARCH_QUESTION
Question: The already-answered PO question ("supply a sample log now or defer to build?" → defer)
named only the **Claude Code** log. Will a scrubbed **Codex** session log
(`~/.codex/sessions/**`, ≥3 `token_count` events from one session) also be supplied at BUILD start?
Options: (A) yes — both Claude and Codex samples at BUILD start; (B) Claude only, and Codex parsing
is built against synthetic fixtures from the documented shape; (C) Claude only, and Codex support
slips to a follow-up phase.
Assuming: **(A)** — listed as prerequisite PRE-2. Two Codex behaviours cannot be settled without a
real file: whether `token_count.total_token_usage` is cumulative per session (summing it would
inflate the daily total several-fold), and whether `input_tokens` includes `cached_input_tokens`
(getting the sign wrong misprices the cache-read bucket by up to 10×).
Impact: If (B), Codex figures ship unverified and acceptance signal 3 ("Codex sessions are counted
and priced from their token fields") can only be tested against our own assumptions — I would then
want the Codex total marked provisional in `lum doctor` until a real log is seen. If (C), Phase 1
ships Claude-only and `clis` defaults to `["claude"]`.

---

## ARCH_QUESTION
Question: When the budget is exceeded on a **subscription** account (where the imputed USD is not
real money), should the amber/red thresholds and notification still fire?
Options: (A) yes — treat the imputed figure as a usage budget and fire normally; (B) no — thresholds
apply only to real marginal spend, and subscription users see the number without colour escalation;
(C) fire, but with different wording ("80% of daily usage allowance" rather than "budget").
Assuming: **(A), with (C)'s wording** — acceptance signal 4 states plainly that crossing 80%/100%
triggers amber then red, with no carve-out for account type, and self-pacing is the stated goal.
Impact: If (B), `imputeCostForSubscription: true` becomes display-only and the entire budget
evaluation path must be gated on `accountMode === "api"` — which would make the tool inert for the
most common Claude Code setup, so I have designed for (A).

ARCH_QUESTION 1 (accountMode): Ratify Option A — add optional per-CLI accountMode with default subscription. Option B (always ≈) misleads API-key users whose cost is exact; Option C (auto-detect via env/credential files) violates the nothing-sensitive posture and is fragile. The two Codex token semantics (cumulative vs delta on total_token_usage; whether input_tokens includes cached_input_tokens) are undecidable without a real multi-event session file — synthetic fixtures just push the verification to after the first real run. Choose A (both Claude and Codex logs at BUILD start) or C (defer Codex to Phase 2, ship Claude-only). Proceeding on Option B (synthetic only) is not recommended.

ARCH_QUESTION 3 (subscription thresholds): Ratify A+C hybrid — fire thresholds at the same fractions for all account types, but substitute usage-allowance wording for subscription accounts (e.g. 80% of daily usage allowance instead of 80% of daily budget). Option B (no thresholds for subscription) would make the meter inert for the most common Claude Code setup, defeating the self-pacing goal. The wording difference is one string interpolation in notify/notifier.ts; no changes to the budget domain function or fraction computation.

CRITICAL: ccusage v20 is a compiled Rust binary with no JS library exports. The PricingPort/BaselineLoaderPort embed strategy in ADR-001 is not implementable. The shell-out adapter must be elevated from escape hatch to primary integration path, OR the design must drop the ccusage runtime dependency and implement direct JSONL parsing + LiteLLM pricing JSON directly. The port abstraction itself is still sound — only which adapter is primary changes.

DESIGN.md establishes the terminal-first design system for local-usage-meter: OLED dark palette (bg #0F172A, fg #F8FAFC), green/amber/red threshold colors (ANSI 77/208/203), JetBrains Mono typography, and component specs for statusline string (≤28 chars), TUI live view (Ink), OS notifications, and lum doctor output.

Design system adopted: OLED dark mode palette as primary (bg #0F172A, text #F8FAFC), JetBrains Mono typography. Three-state threshold color system: normal <80% = green ANSI 208, warning 80-99% = amber ANSI 208, over >=100% = red ANSI 203. Statusline hard-capped at 28 chars. Subscription accounts use ≈ prefix + muted color; notification wording uses "usage allowance" (A+C hybrid ratified). TUI uses Ink (React-for-CLI) with file-watch-only redraws.

core-pipeline: Build the full data pipeline from raw JSONL logs to an atomic daily snapshot, including repo scaffold, domain types, JSONL readers, pricing (LiteLLM-direct or ccusage shell-out primary — ccusage v20 is a Rust binary, embed strategy not viable), deduplication, watch daemon, reconciler, and the `lum today` one-shot command.

Scope: Covers PRE-8 (repo scaffold: package.json, tsconfig, vitest, biome, CI), domain/ (TokenCounts, TurnRecord, DailyLedger, Snapshot, Config, ports), adapters/readers (claude-jsonl, codex-jsonl, tail, discovery), adapters/ccusage (pricing via LiteLLM JSON or shell-out — choose primary adapter as first build decision), adapters/watch (chokidar primary + safety poll), adapters/store (atomic-json, lockfile, paths), app/ (LedgerService, WatchOrchestrator, Reconciler, SnapshotWriter), and bin/lum.ts with `lum today` subcommand. Also covers PRE-3 through PRE-7 (builder VERIFY steps against real sample logs). NOT in scope: statusline script, budget thresholds/notifications, live TUI, lum doctor.

Done when:
- `lum today` prints `today $X / $BUDGET (P%)` with correct per-CLI breakdown against the real sample logs
- Dedup test passes: same assistant message in two .jsonl files counts once
- Codex cumulative-vs-delta test passes (token_count events correctly delta-ed)
- Parity test passes: |our total − ccusage total| ≤ max($0.01, 0.5%) for both Claude and Codex fixtures
- Offline CI gate green: full suite runs with sockets stubbed to throw

statusline-and-alerts: Deliver the Claude Code statusline integration and the budget threshold alert system — the two user-facing real-time surfaces that fire from the daemon-written snapshot.

Scope: Covers bin/statusline.js (standalone, node:fs only, < 30 ms, always-exit-0), render/statusline.ts (snapshot → single ANSI line), daemon liveness check and self-spawn throttle (§6.4), lum install-statusline (patch ~/.claude/settings.json), domain/budget.ts (evaluate fraction/state), app/ThresholdLatch (amber/red, once-per-day, persisted in thresholdsFired), adapters/notify/notifier.ts (osascript / notify-send / PowerShell / bell fallback), amber/red ANSI colors per DESIGN.md, subscription ≈ prefix and usage-allowance wording (A+C hybrid). NOT in scope: live TUI, breakdown table, lum doctor, lum service install.

Done when:
- Statusline renders correctly in real Claude Code (manual end-to-end verification)
- p95 latency < 30 ms over 200 invocations (CI latency test)
- Exit code is 0 on every fault: missing snapshot, corrupt snapshot, stale snapshot, no daemon (fault-injection tests)
- Crossing 80% then 100% fires amber then red display plus exactly one notification each; daemon restart does not re-fire (acceptance signal 4)

breakdown-ui: Deliver the full breakdown and diagnostic surfaces — the `lum --live` full-screen TUI, the `lum today` per-CLI/per-model breakdown table, `lum doctor`, and `lum service install` — that complete the v1 product surface on top of the shared snapshot written by the daemon.

Scope: Covers render/live.ts (`lum --live` full-screen ANSI dashboard, redraws on snapshot file change, no Ink/React runtime), render/table.ts (per-CLI and per-model breakdown table for `lum today` with imputed label), lum doctor (snapshot age, watch mode, pricing version, unknown models, parse errors, last drift), lum service install|uninstall (launchd on macOS, systemd --user on Linux). All rendering reads only the Snapshot type frozen at the core-pipeline boundary — no direct ledger or log file access. NOT in scope: statusline, threshold notifications, the daemon itself, any ccusage or JSONL parsing.

Done when:
- `lum --live` redraws within 1 s of snapshot change; Ctrl-C exits cleanly with terminal restored
- Per-CLI and per-model figures in `lum today` table sum exactly to the total USD
- `lum doctor` correctly surfaces: stale snapshot, no-daemon, unknown-model, parse-errors, last drift, watch mode, pricing snapshot version
- `lum service install` creates a working launchd (macOS) or systemd --user (Linux) unit; `lum service uninstall` removes it cleanly
